title: SNO 2002: neutral-current flux and a non-electron component 5.3 sigma from zero
summary: SNO reports an electron-neutrino flux 1.76 × 10^6 cm^−2 s^−1 and a non-electron component 5.3 standard deviations above zero. The total flux is compared with solar models.
body: The SNO collaboration abstract reports neutral-current neutrino interactions on deuterium. Assuming the standard boron-8 spectrum shape, and a kinetic-energy threshold of 5 MeV, the electron-neutrino component is 1.76 ± 0.05 (stat.) ± 0.09 (syst.) × 10^6 cm^−2 s^−1. The non-electron component is 3.41 ± 0.45 (stat.) +0.48/−0.45 (syst.) × 10^6 cm^−2 s^−1, which the abstract says is 5.3 standard deviations greater than zero, and calls that strong evidence for solar electron-neutrino flavor transformation. The total flux from the neutral-current reaction is 5.09 +0.44/−0.43 (stat.) +0.46/−0.43 (syst.) × 10^6 cm^−2 s^−1, which the abstract says is consistent with solar models. The fluxes are the measurement. Consistency with solar models is a comparison to a model, not the model itself.
